g.text: SO-101 tool changer, exploded
Arm side (master) on the left, tool coupler in the middle, dock on the right. Drawn in the locked orientation, pulled apart along the coupling axis.
Every printed part, screw, insert, dowel, ball, spring and magnet is numbered below with its size. Orange = dock retrofit kit. Concept render from the current CAD, not a photo.
Parts
roll-servo horn (existing SO-101 arm part, context only) [bought]
4x M3x6 button screw, hub to roll horn [bought]
hub, printed PLA
2x M3 heat-set insert in hub, 4.0 bore x 6.7 [bought]
2x M3x40 socket-head screw, cage to hub [bought]
back pad, printed TPU
STS3215 servo + gripper horn, bought (box = nominal 45.4 x 24.8 x 35.4; mesh not in repo)
hold-down strap, printed PLA
far pad shim, printed TPU
2x M3x8 button screw, strap to cage [bought]
2x M3 heat-set insert in cage boss [bought]
cage, printed PLA
3x M3x8 button screw, ring to cage [bought]
3x M3 heat-set insert in ring top, 4.0 bore x 6.7 [bought]
3x spring, 5 mm OD x 0.7 wire x 10 mm free [bought]
3x ball plunger, printed PLA
3x steel ball 5/32 in (3.97 mm) [bought]
6x steel dowel 3 x 12, glued in the V grooves [bought]
coupling ring, printed PLA
lead-in skirt, printed PLA (CA glue)
blade carrier + blade, printed PLA
4x M3x5 button screw, carrier to gripper horn [bought]
tool body + square neck, printed PLA (GT1 gripper shown)
body cover, printed PLA
4x M3 heat-set insert in neck, 4.0 bore x 6.7 [bought]
N52 magnet 6 x 3, sealed in the neck underside [bought]
coupling plate + spigot, printed PLA
3x steel dowel 3 x 12, glued in plate [bought]
4x M3x10 countersunk screw, plate to neck [bought]
floating rotor, printed PLA
dock post, printed PLA (drawn ghosted)
N52 magnet 6 x 3, in the floor land (1 mm deep) [bought]
2x stop pad D10 x 1.6, printed
2x tape disc D10 x 0.4 [bought]
2x cradle column, printed
2x tape strip 23.6 x 14.8 x 0.4 [bought]

Not drawn here: the T-gauge, thread and R2 head option (see the dock diagram). The tool body is the GT1 gripper (its jaws and cover screws are not itemised in the BOM). Hardware sizes nominal. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
